correctness.rationale: The gap lemma holds for any profile and gives the necessary strict score inequality between sincere weight, opponent-score difference and deviating weight. For m<=3 attainable differences lie on a (3/2)-lattice and exclude the only open interval; m1, m2 are immediate. Exact Fraction exhaustive check covers every ordered 4-candidate ballot report for n=1..3, yielding zero cases; explicit 4-voter witness verified exactly with strict winning A then B. These finite checks are not extrapolated to larger electorates.

evidence: Section 2.5 of arXiv:2505.01395v1 gives equivalent disapproval point rule and optimum scoring weights.
Both formulations induce precisely the same winner set because each nonempty, nonfull ballot distributes constant total point sum.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The theorem is invariant under the dual disapproval-weighted minimizing formulation and positive common rescaling. Original Section 2.5 establishes representation guarantees for both, not strict-to-strict strategic boundary. Old plain approval rule has ballot-independent weight and does not imply this threshold.

value.rationale: Locates the first tie-independent profitable approval-padding deviation in a recently proposed FVR-optimal voting mechanism: all electorates with <=3 candidates are immune to this strict defect, 4-candidate elections first fail at four voters. Structural explanation via the score lattice and a concrete FVR-representation-versus-incentives boundary motivate this exact threshold.
